title: Kimi No Longer Just Writes Proposals: It Directly Modifies Unity and Unreal Projects to Build Game Prototypes
excerpt: On November 2, Moonshot AI released its "Game Development and Creative Work Solutions." It is built on the Kimi K3.1 series models, plus the large-mod
content_html:
On November 2, Moonshot AI released its "Game Development and Creative Work Solutions." It is built on the Kimi K3.1 series models, plus the large-model coding product Kimi Code and the agent product Kimi Work, and connects with professional plugins such as Unity, Unreal Engine, and Blender. What makes it most different is that it no longer just outputs a paragraph of text or an image. Instead, it directly connects to a team's existing workflow, operates editors, rewrites existing projects, and delivers files that can continue to be edited along with operation logs.

Two Longstanding Barriers: Gameplay Is Hard to Validate, Roles Are Hard to Coordinate

The game industry has long been stuck in two places. First, to judge whether a gameplay idea is fun, you really have to build it and try it out—but building prototypes takes time and manpower, so teams often only dare validate a few ideas. Kimi can help churn out several more prototype versions within a limited window, allowing more directions to be compared side by side. Second, designers' ideas need to be translated into engineering tasks, and art assets still need to align with engine specifications. If AI only provides half-finished products, teams still have to spend a lot of effort adapting them.

The Trio Has a Clear Division of Labor, and Match-3 Card Games Become a Showcase

In execution, the model is responsible for understanding goals, planning, and assigning tasks; Kimi Code focuses on code development and modifications; Kimi Work takes on cross-file, multi-step production. Take "adding freely combinable rule cards to a match-3 game" as an example. Kimi first sorts out how rule stacking affects elimination strategies, scoring, and feedback, then breaks it down into specific tasks such as interaction, numbers, UI, and audiovisual elements, and produces a playable prototype. Through plugin calls, it can now directly work on existing projects in Blender, Unity, and Unreal, pushing game and 3D creation one step forward.
